source.method: straight-line fit to the published characteristic curve over one log H window shared by all three channels, [0.78, 2.68], on the sheet's own relative log exposure axis, anchored to Kodak's lux-second axis at the sheet's printed ISO 125/22° through the ISO 5800 speed point (green and the slower of red and blue, each at minimum density plus 0.15, reached at relative log H 1.029), a shift of -2.98, which makes the window Kodak's [-2.2, -0.3]
source.publication: Harman Phoenix 125 technical data sheet H26

name: Harman Phoenix 125
note: Dye gammas are this stock's own, read off its maker's published characteristic curve. Nothing here is measured from a roll. Its own emulsion as far as its maker says: Harman's sheet ties it to no other stock, although the curve it prints is the same figure as on the Phoenix 200 sheet. The sheet's speed line reads ISO 125/22° with EI 200 in the same sentence, and the anchor uses the ISO 125.
